pr_body:
Soft expects will still fail the test, but will not abort it's execution. As a consequence of this:
-  `TestResult` now might have multiple errors, which is reflected with a new `testResult.erros: TestError[]` field.
- `TestInfo` now might have multiple errors as well, which is reflected with a new `testInfo.errors: TestError[]` field.

This is how multiple `expect.soft` look in HTML report:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/746130/152091581-e6b1d882-adca-4839-9584-8560e977c118.png)

These are the same soft errors in terminal:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/746130/152091660-f6070eff-4dd5-48ed-b0d2-7920e0456d2e.png)
 
Fixes #7819

issue_context.title: [Feature]: Soft/queued asserts/expects so that it does not fail after the first one
issue_context.body:
### Your question

I have a scenario where we have multiple scenarios to assert. I want to finish off all assertions irrespective of their status and need to see what all assertions got passed or failed once all validations steps were done. 
Is there any way to do this in Playwright?
comments: I did not find any soft assert wrappers for `expect`, but this is a popular request, so we'll do that.
maybe instead of "soft assert", it would be queued asserts? Would seem easier to implement.

IMHO this feature or something like this #7786 would be one of the determinant factors to choose Playwright runner for people who think of migrating from legacy frameworks which use Jasmine soft assertions (Protractor, for example) or people that worked previously with Java frameworks where TestNG soft assertion was widely used. At my company I told several people about Playwright and they were pretty excited, but the absence of soft assertions stopped them to consider this tool further and do the leap of faith 🙂

(Not needing this myself (yet?) but stumbled on the issue and thought I'd share some examples)

In case you're looking for examples how it looks in other assertion libraries:
https://fluentassertions.com/introduction#assertion-scopes
https://docs.nunit.org/articles/nunit/writing-tests/assertions/multiple-asserts.html
(Both are examples from .NET)

And now as I'm browsing through our existing Protractor tests, I see we are working around chai limitations there by having one dedicated "it" block (test) per assertion. So the action is done in a previous "it" block, and the assertions follow each in their own separate "it" block. That wouldn't work in @playwright/test.

So I think we need this after all.
This feature would be very useful for my company as well.  Not a deal breaker to not have it but would be greatly appreciated if this could be added at some point :)
